races.title: State House, District 87
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Destin Hall
cands.bio: Republican attorney from Lenoir, serving in the North Carolina House since 2017 for District 87 (Caldwell and Watauga counties). Elected Speaker of the House in January 2025. Partner at Wilson, Lackey, Rohr & Hall, P.C. Earlier chaired the House Rules Committee.
cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Hall on data centers or on development and growth limits. We found nothing on homestead property tax relief specifically, only general statements about cutting taxes. We found no sourced record of what he did on restrictions on investor or foreign land buying, school choice or teacher pay, police pay and pensions, or other specific bills. A Wikipedia page lists House Bill 370 (cooperation with ICE detainers) as notable legislation, but it does not say whether Hall sponsored it or voted on it, so it is left out. Ballotpedia shows no endorsements for him in 2024 or 2026, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so his platform positions are thinly documented. His 'roots' score rests on Wikipedia's account of his upbringing.

local.label: Roots 100: Born in Lenoir, raised mostly by his grandparents and a graduate of West Caldwell High School, he practiced in Charlotte for a year after law school, then returned to Lenoir and Caldwell County.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Practicing attorney (associate at SeiferFlatow, partner at Fleischer & Hall and then Wilson, Lackey, Rohr & Hall). State House member since 2017 and Speaker since January 2025. Elected Majority Freshman Leader of the House Republican Caucus in 2017.
qual.why: Nine years of legislative service, current chamber leadership as Speaker, and a law career put him in the top band for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: Nine years of legislative service, current chamber leadership as Speaker, and a law career put him in the top band for writing law and the state budget.

workers-first.evidence: In his response to Gov. Stein's 2025 State of the State address, Hall listed among Republican accomplishments 'rejecting the Democrats' dangerous sanctuary policies that protect illegal aliens from justice.'

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says his legislative priorities include the staunch defense of Second Amendment rights.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says his legislative priorities include defending pro-life issues.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

roots.summary: Born in Lenoir, raised mostly by his grandparents and a graduate of West Caldwell High School, he practiced in Charlotte for a year after law school, then returned to Lenoir and Caldwell County.

cands.name: Iris Bender
cands.bio: Lenoir, North Carolina small business owner and mother. Holds a degree in Business and Marketing. Her family left Cuba in 1998. Ran as the Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 87 in 2026. No elected office held, per Ballotpedia.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended by three Sway voting groups: Bull City Anna's Voting Group, Imani's Pix, and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy.

cands.gaps: We could not confirm Iris Bender's birthplace. Her campaign says she was born and raised in a Cuban family that left Cuba in 1998, but it does not name a place of birth or where she grew up. We found no record of prior elected office, legislative work, or detailed business history, such as the name or type of her business. We found no statements or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, or abortion. Her only stated positions on the topics we track concern vouchers and teacher pay.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign site says she and her husband made Caldwell County home nearly two decades ago, after her family left Cuba in 1998, which places her arrival in NC as an adult 10-25 years ago.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Small business owner with a degree in Business and Marketing, earned while working full time. She has volunteered with local schools and special-needs families. No prior elected office is listed.
qual.why: Business ownership and management put her in the middle band. No legislative, local elected, law, policy or budget work is documented.
qual.label: Business ownership and management put her in the middle band. No legislative, local elected, law, policy or budget work is documented.

roots.summary: Her campaign site says she and her husband made Caldwell County home nearly two decades ago, after her family left Cuba in 1998, which places her arrival in NC as an adult 10-25 years ago.
